channel.title: How to End War and Disease
channel.description: The Complete Idiot's Guide to Legally Bribing Your Way to Utopia

item.title: Your Money Comes From a Building and They Use It to Kill People
item.description: Your money is manufactured in a building by people you didn't elect. It has funded unpopular wars that killed 97 million people. They give it to their friends first, then use the rest to buy weapons you didn't ask for. By the time it reaches you, it buys less. This has been happening for a century. Nobody covers it on the news because it is, by design, extremely boring.

item.title: Why Your National Institutes of Health Fails to Institute Health
item.description: A root cause analysis of why the world's largest medical research institution converts 3.3% of its budget into testing which of the thousands of known-safe treatments actually work in humans. Oxford tested COVID treatments for $500 per patient and saved a million lives in 100 days. The NIH spent $1.6 billion and completed zero. The humans inside the system are not the problem. The system is the problem.

item.title: The Cost of War
item.description: Quantifying Human Idiocy - A precise accounting of what humans spend to destroy themselves, with numbers that would make a statistician weep.

item.title: The FDA Is Unsafe and Ineffective
item.description: A drug passes every safety test your species invented. It won't kill you. Everyone agrees. You still can't have it for another because a committee needs to confirm it works well enough. You could volunteer for the trials that would answer that question faster, but the system has slots for patients. There is, however, no waiting list for dying. This is the agency standing between the treaty's money and actual cured diseases.

item.title: The Cautionary Tale of Moronia
item.description: A planet had every tool needed to cure disease and chose to build weapons instead. They went extinct. Their last words were 'but the economy.' This is a bedtime story for civilizations that can't do math.

item.title: Genetic Slavery
item.description: Your government spends more on weapons than on curing disease, and you think that's a political problem. It's not. It's a hardware problem. You're running 200,000-year-old software optimized for hoarding rocks and fearing strangers, and you've given it nuclear weapons. This chapter is the owner's manual for the brain that's trying to kill you.
